title: Food waste
paragraphs: How much food do you buy each week? Are you someone who stuffs your fridge and cupboards full of edible treats so that you‘ll always have something to munch on and so that you’ll never go hungry? Or maybe, like me, you‘re more efficient with your shopping, only buying what you need and using up your leftovers so that you keep food waste to a minimum.

Throwing away unwanted food has become a big issue in the developed world. While some of us chuck away unwanted items, people in other parts of world face food shortages and are starving. It’s a shocking fact that a third of the world‘s food is wasted each year. The actual figure is 1.3 billion tons of food, which is enough to feed a billion hungry people.

You might think supermarkets are the main contributors to this mountain of waste. After all, they do discard stuff that has passed its sell-by-date, and they often refuse to sell vegetables or fruit that are oddly shaped or look damaged. They’ve also been criticised for encouraging customers to buy more than they need through promotions such as ‘buy one get one free‘.

But the biggest culprit for creating food waste is us. In Europe an incredible 53% of food waste comes from households, which results in 88 million tonnes of food waste a year. So instead of filling our bellies, our food is filling up landfill sites — it’s buried and left to rot. Unfortunately this causes greenhouse gases which eventually leads to global warming and climate change.

In Denmark, a woman called Selina Juul has been working hard to tackle this problem. She moved from Russia many years ago and was amazed to see the abundance of food available in the supermarkets. But despite so much availability, she found that people were buying more than they needed and throwing too much away.

She convinced some supermarkets to stop selling their items in bulk so that people bought only what they needed. She produced a leftovers cookbook and she‘s now set up an education programme in schools. This has helped create a significant 25% reduction in food waste, which shows that something can be done.

Clearly, we need to think twice when we put something in our shopping trolley, and when we’re at home we should make the most of the food we have - using recipes that use up our leftovers or even sharing our excess food with our friends and neighbours.

vocabulary.entry: stuff [v.] /stʌf/ 填满；塞满 (口语)
vocabulary.example: She stuffed her suitcase with clothes.
vocabulary.translation: 她把衣服塞满了手提箱。

vocabulary.entry: edible [adj.] /ˈedəbəl/ 可食用的
vocabulary.example: These mushrooms are edible but those are poisonous.
vocabulary.translation: 这些蘑菇是可食用的，但那些是有毒的。

vocabulary.entry: munch on [phr.] /mʌntʃ ɒn/ 用力咀嚼；津津有味地吃 (口语)
vocabulary.example: He was munching on an apple while reading.
vocabulary.translation: 他一边看书一边津津有味地啃着苹果。

vocabulary.entry: leftovers [n. pl.] /ˈleftəʊvəz/ 剩菜；剩饭 (口语；单数: leftover)
vocabulary.example: We ate leftovers for dinner.
vocabulary.translation: 我们晚餐吃了剩菜。

vocabulary.entry: chuck away [phr.] /tʃʌk əˈweɪ/ 扔掉；丢弃 (口语)
vocabulary.example: Don‘t chuck away those old books.
vocabulary.translation: 别扔掉那些旧书。

vocabulary.entry: feed [v.] /fiːd/ 养活；供养
vocabulary.example: The farm feeds the whole village.
vocabulary.translation: 这个农场养活整个村庄。

vocabulary.entry: contributor [n.] /kənˈtrɪbjʊtə/ 促成因素；贡献者 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: Exhaust fumes are a major contributor to air pollution.
vocabulary.translation: 废气是空气污染的主要促成因素。

vocabulary.entry: discard [v.] /dɪsˈkɑːd/ 丢弃；抛弃 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: Please discard any expired food.
vocabulary.translation: 请丢弃任何过期的食物。

vocabulary.entry: sell-by-date [n.] /ˈsel baɪ deɪt/ 保质期；销售截止日期
vocabulary.example: Check the sell-by-date before buying milk.
vocabulary.translation: 买牛奶前检查一下保质期。

vocabulary.entry: culprit [n.] /ˈkʌlprɪt/ 罪魁祸首；引起问题的事物 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The main culprit of the fire was faulty wiring.
vocabulary.translation: 火灾的主要原因是电线故障。

vocabulary.entry: fill up [phr.] /fɪl ʌp/ 填满；装满
vocabulary.example: Please fill up the tank with petrol.
vocabulary.translation: 请把油箱加满汽油。

vocabulary.entry: tackle [v.] /ˈtækəl/ 处理；解决
vocabulary.example: The government must tackle climate change.
vocabulary.translation: 政府必须解决气候变化问题。

vocabulary.entry: abundance [n.] /əˈbʌndəns/ 丰富；大量 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: There is an abundance of fresh fruit in summer.
vocabulary.translation: 夏天有大量的新鲜水果。

vocabulary.entry: convince [v.] /kənˈvɪns/ 说服；使确信
vocabulary.example: She convinced me to take the job.
vocabulary.translation: 她说服我接受了这份工作。

vocabulary.entry: in bulk [phr.] /ɪn bʌlk/ 大量；整批
vocabulary.example: Buying in bulk can save money.
vocabulary.translation: 批量购买可以省钱。

vocabulary.entry: think twice [phr.] /θɪŋk twaɪs/ 三思；慎重考虑
vocabulary.example: You should think twice before making a decision.
vocabulary.translation: 做决定前你应该三思。

vocabulary.entry: make the most of [phr.] /meɪk ðə məʊst əv/ 充分利用
vocabulary.example: We should make the most of every opportunity.
vocabulary.translation: 我们应该充分利用每一个机会。

vocabulary.entry: excess [adj.] /ˈekses/ 多余的；过量的
vocabulary.example: The excess food was donated to a shelter.
vocabulary.translation: 多余的食物被捐赠给了收容所。

vocabulary.entry: landfill site [n.] /ˈlændfɪl saɪt/ 垃圾填埋场

vocabulary.translation: 这些废物被运往垃圾填埋场。

vocabulary.entry: starve [v.] /stɑːv/ 挨饿；饿死

vocabulary.translation: 这个地区有成千上万的人在挨饿。

vocabulary.translation: 二氧化碳是一种温室气体。

vocabulary.entry: global warming [n.] /ˌɡləʊbəl ˈwɔːmɪŋ/ 全球变暖

vocabulary.translation: 全球变暖对地球是一个严重的威胁。

vocabulary.entry: promotion [n.] /prəˈməʊʃən/ 促销活动
vocabulary.example: The store is running a promotion on coffee.
vocabulary.translation: 这家商店正在进行咖啡促销活动。

vocabulary.entry: buy one get one free [phr.] /baɪ wʌn ɡet wʌn friː/ 买一送一 (口语)
vocabulary.example: The supermarket offers buy one get one free on selected items.
vocabulary.translation: 这家超市对特定商品提供买一送一的优惠。

vocabulary.entry: cookbook [n.] /ˈkʊkbʊk/ 食谱；烹饪书
vocabulary.example: She bought a vegetarian cookbook.
vocabulary.translation: 她买了一本素食食谱。

sentences.english: How much food do you buy each week?
sentences.chinese: 你每周买多少食物呢？

sentences.english: Are you someone who stuffs your fridge and cupboards full of edible treats so that you‘ll always have something to munch on and so that you’ll never go hungry?
sentences.chinese: 你是不是那种把冰箱和橱柜都塞满可食用的美味食品的人，这样你就总是有东西可以咀嚼，而且永远不会挨饿呢？

sentences.english: Or maybe, like me, you‘re more efficient with your shopping, only buying what you need and using up your leftovers so that you keep food waste to a minimum.
sentences.chinese: 或者，也许像我一样，你在购物方面更有效率，只买你需要的东西，把剩菜剩饭都吃光，以便将食物浪费降到最低限度。

sentences.english: Throwing away unwanted food has become a big issue in the developed world.
sentences.chinese: 在发达国家，扔掉不需要的食物已经成为一个大问题。

sentences.english: While some of us chuck away unwanted items, people in other parts of world face food shortages and are starving.
sentences.chinese: 当我们中的一些人扔掉不需要的东西时，世界其他地区的人们却面临着食物短缺，正在挨饿。

sentences.english: It’s a shocking fact that a third of the world‘s food is wasted each year.
sentences.chinese: 一个令人震惊的事实是，世界上每年有三分之一的食物被浪费掉。

sentences.english: The actual figure is 1.3 billion tons of food, which is enough to feed a billion hungry people.
sentences.chinese: 实际数字是13亿吨食物，这足以养活10亿饥饿的人。

sentences.english: You might think supermarkets are the main contributors to this mountain of waste.
sentences.chinese: 你可能会认为超市是造成这堆积如山的食物浪费的主要促成因素。

sentences.english: After all, they do discard stuff that has passed its sell-by-date, and they often refuse to sell vegetables or fruit that are oddly shaped or look damaged.
sentences.chinese: 毕竟，他们确实会丢弃那些过了保质期的东西，而且他们经常拒绝出售形状不好或看起来有损坏的蔬菜或水果。

sentences.english: They’ve also been criticised for encouraging customers to buy more than they need through promotions such as ‘buy one get one free‘.
sentences.chinese: 他们还因为通过“买一送一”等促销活动鼓励顾客购买超过他们需要的东西而受到批评。

sentences.english: But the biggest culprit for creating food waste is us.
sentences.chinese: 但造成食物浪费的最大罪魁祸首是我们自己。

sentences.english: In Europe an incredible 53% of food waste comes from households, which results in 88 million tonnes of food waste a year.
sentences.chinese: 在欧洲，令人难以置信的是，53%的食物浪费来自家庭，这导致每年产生8800万吨的食物浪费。

sentences.english: So instead of filling our bellies, our food is filling up landfill sites — it’s buried and left to rot.
sentences.chinese: 所以，我们的食物不是填饱我们的肚子，而是填满了垃圾填埋场——它们被掩埋起来任其腐烂。

sentences.english: Unfortunately this causes greenhouse gases which eventually leads to global warming and climate change.
sentences.chinese: 不幸的是，这会产生温室气体，最终导致全球变暖和气候变化。

sentences.english: In Denmark, a woman called Selina Juul has been working hard to tackle this problem.
sentences.chinese: 在丹麦，一位名叫塞琳娜·尤尔的女士一直在努力解决这个问题。

sentences.english: She moved from Russia many years ago and was amazed to see the abundance of food available in the supermarkets.
sentences.chinese: 她多年前从俄罗斯搬到这里，惊讶于超市里食物的丰富多样。

sentences.english: But despite so much availability, she found that people were buying more than they needed and throwing too much away.
sentences.chinese: 但是，尽管有这么多的食物，她发现人们购买远超他们所需要的食物，而且也扔掉了太多的食物。

sentences.english: She convinced some supermarkets to stop selling their items in bulk so that people bought only what they needed.
sentences.chinese: 她说服了一些超市停止批量地销售商品，这样人们就只购买他们需要的东西。

sentences.english: She produced a leftovers cookbook and she‘s now set up an education programme in schools.
sentences.chinese: 她制作了一本剩菜食谱，现在她还在学校设立了一个教育项目。

sentences.english: This has helped create a significant 25% reduction in food waste, which shows that something can be done.
sentences.chinese: 这使得食物浪费显著减少了25%，这表明我们是可以有所作为的。

sentences.english: Clearly, we need to think twice when we put something in our shopping trolley, and when we’re at home we should make the most of the food we have - using recipes that use up our leftovers or even sharing our excess food with our friends and neighbours.
sentences.chinese: 显然，当我们把东西放进购物车的时候，我们需要三思而后行，而当我们在家的时候，我们应该充分利用我们所拥有的食物——使用可以把剩菜用光的食谱，甚至可以和我们的朋友和邻居分享我们多余的食物。
